title: The Religious Portions of the Book of Poetry
attributionNote: The collection gathered court and folk songs, dynastic hymns and sacrificial odes over several centuries. Tradition says Confucius edited the collection down to its present three hundred and five odes; the received text was fixed in the Han.
description: The Book of Poetry is the classic of Chinese verse: the airs of the fifteen states, the minor and greater odes of the royal domain, and the sacrificial hymns of Zhou. Its songs of courtship, marriage, war, harvest, feasting and mourning were read by Confucian commentators as moral allegory and are the foundation of Chinese poetry. Legge prints the odes with their religious portions and his own notes.
historicalContext: The odes were memorised and quoted by every educated man, and the tradition of reading them as moral instruction runs from the Zuo commentary to Zhu Xi. Legge's translation with the Chinese text forms the Shih King of the Sacred Books of the East, volume 3 (1879), whose prolegomena trace the collection's formation.
availabilityNote: Selected: the religious odes and hymns that Legge printed in the Sacred Books of the East, with his introductory sections, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed ode or section per chapter. The translator's prolegomena are volume apparatus and are not part of the work. His complete Book of Poetry of 1876 is a separate work in this library.
